question: Which layer of the soil has maximum concentration of humus?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Top Soil.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Top Soil:-**

 
 
• **The layer of soil with the maximum concentration of humus is the topsoil. **
 
• The topsoil is the topmost layer of soil, and it is made up of a mixture of organic matter and mineral matter.
 
• The organic matter in the topsoil comes from decaying plant and animal matter, and it is this organic matter that gives the topsoil its dark color and its nutrient-rich properties.
 
• The amount of humus in the topsoil varies depending on a number of factors, including the type of vegetation that grows in the area, the climate, and the management practices used on the land. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Soil is a complex mixture of minerals, organic matter, water, and air.
 
• It is essential for life on Earth, as it provides plants with the nutrients they need to grow and reproduce.
 
• Soil also plays an important role in water filtration, climate regulation, and carbon storage.
